title: GoFundMe says unauthorized party accessed GoFundMe Pro donor and supporter data
date_note: The NonProfit Times (19 November) reports GoFundMe began notifying affected people by email on 19 November. IBTimes UK, citing GoFundMe's 20 November notice, gives access windows of 10-18 October and 8-9 November; the date here is the disclosure.
geo_basis: country: The NonProfit Times reports notification by mail in North Dakota and Washington and to those states' regulators; no headquarters city stated on the pages read
summary: GoFundMe says an unauthorized third party accessed donor and supporter information on GoFundMe Pro, The NonProfit Times and Fortune report. Per GoFundMe's customer email, the data included names, addresses, phone numbers and dates of birth, and for some organisations Salesforce credentials. Salesforce disabled the GoFundMe Pro connected app. Per WPXI, GoFundMe says it addressed the known access methods and reported the incident to law enforcement.
plain: GoFundMe says an unauthorized party gained access to donor and supporter information on GoFundMe Pro, a fundraising service for charities, including names, addresses, emails, phone numbers and birth dates.
exec: Unauthorized access at a nonprofit fundraising platform reached donor contact details and, for some charities, Salesforce integration credentials.
action: As The NonProfit Times advises, GoFundMe Pro Salesforce integration users should rotate all keys and credentials stored in Salesforce and review the Setup Audit Trail and Login History for unfamiliar activity; Salesforce has disabled the GoFundMe Pro connected app.
impact: Donor and supporter names, postal addresses, email addresses, phone numbers and dates of birth; Salesforce integration credentials for some organisations (per GoFundMe's customer email, relayed by Fortune).

sources.name: The NonProfit Times: Update: AI Bot Attacks Did Access Some Donor Data

validation.note: The NonProfit Times and Fortune each quote a GoFundMe spokesperson confirming unauthorized access to GoFundMe Pro; data categories from GoFundMe's customer email as relayed by Fortune; Salesforce statement from NPT. GoFundMe's own notice was not read. No attacker named. DonorPerfect's separate incident is not part of this record.
